scenarios.title: A clinician can see today's work on arrival
scenarios.acceptance: The first screen names who is late and who is due today.

scenarios.title: A nurse records a contact attempt and the record shows who and what
scenarios.acceptance: Reaching the patient moves the record to Reminded and appends an audit row naming the nurse.

scenarios.title: An unanswered call leaves the record scheduled with the attempt counted
scenarios.acceptance: Only "reached" advances the status; the attempt is still recorded.

scenarios.title: Rescheduling supersedes the queued reminder
scenarios.acceptance: A moved date increments the revision and marks the old reminder obsolete, so the patient is not chased twice.

scenarios.title: A closed record cannot be disclosed, and the refusal is explained
scenarios.acceptance: The send is refused with a code and a sentence a clinician can act on, not a generic server error.

observed.message: A closed follow-up cannot be disclosed.

scenarios.title: Only a doctor can close a follow-up
scenarios.acceptance: The server refuses the role, not just the interface, and returns a traceable request id.

scenarios.title: The disclosure shows the exact bytes that would leave, and what stays
scenarios.acceptance: A clinician can see the minimised payload before deciding, including the field list that never leaves.

scenarios.title: Bad input and unknown routes answer safely and traceably
scenarios.acceptance: A caller gets a code and a request id, and nothing internal leaks.
